base.name: ENet
base.note: Stock ENet interoperates: the header, the constants and the commands are the release's own. A client abandons a connection whose verify connect states another channel count, or other throttle values, than its connect asked for.

header.name: sessionId
header.note: The four bytes the client put in its connect command, carried unchanged on every packet. A client drops a packet carrying any other four.

bits.name: peerId
bits.note: 32767 marks an unassigned peer, which is what a connecting client sends. A server gives the client peer 0.

bits.name: sentTimeFlag
bits.note: Set when the header carries a sent time.

constants.name: maximumPeerId
constants.note: Follows from the peer id occupying fifteen bits.

constants.name: maximumTransmissionUnit
constants.note: A client asks for 1400 in its connect command, and takes datagrams up to 4096 bytes.

constants.name: minimumDatagram
constants.note: A client discards any datagram shorter than this many bytes.

base.name: ENet
base.note: Stock ENet does not interoperate. The header below replaces the stock one: it has no checksum and nothing before the session id. The constants replace stock values, and the connect command carries its peer id and session id in one byte each, which spec/transport.md sets out. Everything else, including reliability, sequencing and fragmentation, is stock behaviour.

header.name: addressCheck
header.note: A CRC-32 over the address the datagram is sent to, written big-endian. The input is ten bytes: the IPv4 address in network order, the UDP port as a little-endian u16, and 98 2e 3f 3c. The register starts at all ones; for each input byte it is shifted left eight bits with the byte placed in the low eight, then XORed with the table entry for the eight bits shifted out; the entry for a value v is v shifted left 24 bits, then eight steps of the polynomial 04c11db7, most significant bit first, with no reflection; at the end the register is inverted. A client sending to 127.0.0.1 port 5000 writes 28 68 bd eb, and to port 5001 fa 71 7c 37. A client does not check the field on what it receives, so a server may write any four bytes; a client does not connect without the field.
